card.name: Modal verbs mid-clause before a predicate
card.fires_on: Modal or auxiliary words (would have, might have, will, be able) and nearby clause-internal spots inside a long sentence, where the main predicate has not yet arrived. Mostly general web prose about hypotheticals or speculation.

modes.label: Modal and auxiliary verbs
modes.description: Auxiliaries after would, might, will or be that await a participle or complement.
modes.example: Within the stockade of the mound, there would<< have>> been a timber tower.

modes.label: Parenthetical or possessive breaks
modes.description: A comma or 's inside an interrupting clause before the sentence continues.
modes.example: The phraseology, which must be David's own<<,>> as well as the title above mentioned,

modes.label: Hedged estimate words
modes.description: Words in hedged claims where the sentence is still open.
modes.example: the reported frequency may be an<< underestimate>>.

card.writes: It slightly suppresses words like tomorrow and someday and promotes either/or-type words, with no clear single effect.
card.plain: It fires in the middle of a sentence on helper verbs like would have or might have, when the main point is still to come.
evidence: Within the stockade of the mound, there would<< have>> been a timber tower.
Scientists said if there is any place on Mars that might<< have>> been ripe for life
I'm sure that with time you<< will>> get used to teaching children
